validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real. The sheet's own current_ref (henergy.com/lng-kukrahati) is a live-site marketing page that mentions Kukrahati only in passing and currently SSL-fails (cert mismatch, hosting misconfig) -- so it does not itself support much, but the wiki's own reference list pointed to a genuine primary document I chased down and read myself: PNGRB pdf/eoi/ng/eoi2018/EOI-NG_HEnergy.pdf, a scanned (image-only, no text layer -- url_verifier's substring check cannot read it, confirmed manually via tesseract OCR) 7-page Expression of Interest dated 15 January 2018, in which H-Energy Private Limited applies under PNGRB Reg. 4(1)/5(6) to lay, build and operate the 'Kukrahati - Itinda Natural Gas Pipeline', origin at the Kukrahati LNG regasification terminal (Purba Medinipur district), route via Sarisha and Neutala (South 24 Parganas) and Minakhan (North 24 Parganas) to a custody-transfer point at Itinda on the India-Bangladesh border, length 'approximately 125 Km', assessed transportable volume 'around 18 mmscmd'. Indianpetroplus.com (17-Oct-2019, live, verified) independently corroborates the same EOI date, length (~125 km), capacity (18 MMSCMD) and adds project cost (Rs 210 crore) and owner (H-Energy Pvt Ltd). A Feb-2021 Economic Times article (verified) on the Kukrahati LNG Terminal deal independently states the terminal's overall build-out 'envisages development of a 125 km long pipeline from Kukrahati to Itinda ... and 225 km long pipeline from Kanaichatta to Shrirampur' -- i.e. two DISTINCT pipeline proposals, not the same pipe (rules out a duplicate/relabel with P2214/P6562). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- a common-carrier natural gas transmission pipeline, exactly the class of asset the EOI was filed under. STATUS/SPEC: the sheet's ProposalYear=2020 is wrong -- both the EOI PDF (dated 15-Jan-2018) and indianpetroplus ('H-Energy was submitted the EOI on January 15, 2018') put it at 2018. The indianpetroplus piece also claims H-Energy 'elicited a PNGRB authorization in August, 2019' for this project, but that claim does not hold up: PNGRB's own current, comprehensive natural-gas-pipeline authorization register (pngrb.gov.in/eng-web/ngpl-auth.html, checked live) lists exactly two H-Energy authorizations ever granted -- Jaigarh-Mangalore (28-06-2016, already GEM's P0931) and Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur (23-07-2019, to 'the Consortium of H-Energy East Coast Private Limited and H-Energy Private Limited' -- this is the authorization behind GEM's P2214/P6562, per that row's own shard, granted to SPV HPPL) -- and the word 'Kukrahati', 'Itinda' or 'KIPL' (the EOI's own internal project code) appears NOWHERE on that page. The Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur authorization documents (A_23072019.pdf, OCR'd -- scanned, url_verifier substring check cannot read it either) do reference Kukrahati, but only as a small '24-inch x 2 km Tie-in Line from Kukrahati to KSPL' feeding the much larger Kanai Chhata trunk network -- confirming Kukrahati's gas is actually routed to market via that different, larger, authorized system, not via a dedicated 125 km line to the Bangladesh border. H-Energy's own website (Wayback 2026-06-10 snapshot, verified), whose live infrastructure/pipelines menu lists exactly three pipeline assets -- Jaigarh-Dabhol, Jaigarh-Mangalore, Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur -- has no Kukrahati-Itinda entry at all, even though its Kukrahati LNG Terminal page states 'We have already been awarded the ... PNGRB authorization for the natural gas pipeline which will connect the LNG terminal to the customers in West Bengal and Western Bangladesh' (singular, and that is the Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur/Panitar authorization, not a separate Kukrahati-Itinda one). Net: the 2018 EOI for the standalone Kukrahati-Itinda route was never converted into a PNGRB authorization and was superseded in practice by the Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur/Panitar system's tie-in spur -- Status=cancelled is the right call, well past the dormancy threshold (EOI 2018, 8 years with zero authorization/construction news), but I found no source that says the words 'cancelled' or 'withdrawn' about this specific EOI, so ShelvedCancelledType should be 'inferred', not 'confirmed'.

fills.researcher_notes: Sheet's existing LengthKnown=125 km matches all three sources exactly: the original EOI ('approximate length ... would be 125 Km'), indianpetroplus ('total length of the pipeline is estimated to be about 125 km'), and the Feb-2021 Economic Times piece ('125 km long pipeline from Kukrahati to Itinda'). EOI PDF is a scanned image (no text layer) -- content confirmed manually via tesseract OCR since url_verifier's substring screen cannot read it; the OK verification above is for HTTP liveness only.
EOI PDF's own 'Assessment of total gas volume for transportation' figure is 'Around 18 mmscmd'; indianpetroplus independently states 'Capacity 18 mmscmd'. Matches sheet exactly.

Indianpetroplus states 'Project Cost: 210 crores' = INR 2,100,000,000, matching the sheet exactly. Only one independent source found for the cost figure specifically (the EOI PDF states H-Energy's own net worth, Rs 209.3 crore, as unrelated eligibility evidence -- not the project cost, and easy to mis-conflate with it, but the two numbers are coincidentally close and distinct in the source text) -- tier medium pending a second corroborating source.

EOI filed solely by H-Energy Private Limited (signed by Abhirup Bhattacharya, Authorised Signatory); indianpetroplus independently names 'H-Energy Private Ltd.' as the sole sponsor. No JV/consortium mentioned for this specific EOI (unlike the later Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur bid, which went to a consortium/SPV) -- 100% single-owner is consistent with both sources.

StartLocation/EndLocation/State/Country were already correct on the sheet and are triple-corroborated (EOI PDF + indianpetroplus + Economic Times all agree on Kukrahati->Itinda, West Bengal, India). The two NEW district-level fields (StartPrefecture/District, EndPrefecture/District) were blank and come from a single source, the EOI PDF: origin at Kukrahati, Purba Medinipur district; route via Sarisha and Neutala (South 24 Parganas district) and Minakhan (North 24 Parganas district); terminus/custody-transfer point at Itinda, North 24 Parganas district, India side of the India-Bangladesh border (a real place -- 'Itinda Road, Basirhat' is a documented locality in North 24 Parganas). Note the Feb-2021 Economic Times piece loosely describes the pipeline as running 'to Itinda in Bangladesh', which conflicts with the EOI's own more precise language ('for custody transfer of RLNG at the India Border'); I trust the primary EOI filing over the newspaper's shorthand, so EndCountryOrArea stays India, unchanged. Tier medium because the new district fields are single-sourced -- flagging rather than treating as fully closed.

This is a CORRECTION, not a blank fill -- the sheet currently shows ProposalYear=2020, which is wrong. The EOI letter itself is dated 15 January 2018 ('Ref: HEPL/BD/PNGRB/KIPL/001 ... January 15, 2018'), and indianpetroplus independently states 'H-Energy was submitted the EOI on January 15, 2018'. No source supports a 2020 proposal date for this pipeline; recommend the sheet be corrected to 2018/January.

Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred is consistent with the status-review finding (dormant since the 2018 EOI, never authorized, superseded by a different pipeline), but per standing rule 2 an 'inferred' value gets no fabricated ref -- leaving this UNRESOLVED rather than inventing a citation.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Confirming cancelled is correct, but via structural evidence rather than a literal cancellation announcement (so ShelvedCancelledType=inferred, not confirmed). Last substantive news coverage of this specific 125 km EOI is indianpetroplus, Oct-2019 ('Further RFQs are expected soon' -- i.e. still pre-authorization at that point). Nothing about it appears afterward. Checked live today (2026-08-10, cited under 2026-06 for the Wayback capture date of the H-Energy page I read): PNGRB's current master authorization register for natural gas pipelines (ngpl-auth.html) lists exactly two H-Energy authorizations ever granted -- Jaigarh-Mangalore (2016, = P0931) and Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur (23-07-2019, = P2214/its successor P6562, confirmed independently by that row's own shard) -- with zero mentions of 'Kukrahati', 'Itinda', or the EOI's internal code 'KIPL' anywhere on the page. H-Energy's own current website (Wayback snapshot 2026-06-10) lists only three pipeline assets in its infrastructure menu (Jaigarh-Dabhol, Jaigarh-Mangalore, Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur) and its Kukrahati LNG Terminal page claims only ONE pipeline authorization connecting that terminal to market -- which per the authorization register is the Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur/Panitar system, reached via a small tie-in spur, not a dedicated 125 km Kukrahati-Itinda line. This is much stronger than ordinary silence-based dormancy inference (the standing PNGRB-absence caveat in the brief is about the monthly NGPL-MIS construction register, which is a different, narrower document than this comprehensive authorization-history page), but it still stops short of a literal 'this EOI was rejected/withdrawn' statement, so I'm using 'inferred' per the controlled vocabulary rather than 'confirmed'. No CancelledYear is being proposed -- there is no dated cancellation event to attach, only an absence of ever-granted authorization stretching from the 2018 EOI to today; fabricating a specific year would violate standing rule 2.

summary: P0935 Kukrahati-Itinda: real 2018 EOI (H-Energy, primary PNGRB doc read via OCR), length/capacity/cost/owner all confirmed and refs added, but ProposalYear is wrong (2020->2018) and the pipeline never received PNGRB authorization -- superseded by the separately-authorized Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur/Panitar system (P2214/P6562), which reaches Kukrahati only via a 2km tie-in spur; Status=cancelled confirmed correct, ShelvedCancelledType should be set to inferred.
